Title: Legislature takes up plan to shield Oregon consumers from data centers’ power costs
Description: Oregon lawmakers are considering House Bill 3546 to protect residential consumers from the rising costs of powering data centers. The bill would classify data centers and cryptocurrency miners as a new utility customer class, giving regulators authority to ensure households and small businesses don't shoulder these costs, and requiring new high-load customers to sign 10-year power purchase contracts. While some tech companies like Google support the idea of multi-year agreements and infrastructure charges, they suggest expanding the bill to cover all large power loads, not just data centers, and including collateral requirements.

Title: Ten things to know about the European Union's new product liability directive

Description: A new survey indicates that nearly 95% of air cargo players anticipate a global rise in airfreight rates, particularly from Asia to the US west coast, primarily due to potential new tariffs. The announcement of a 25% levy on foreign-made mobile phones in the US by former President Trump is expected to cause a surge in smartphone imports, leading to tighter transpacific capacity and pushing up rates. Despite a previous decline in smartphone and laptop tonnages, global airfreight rates are already increasing, with a notable rise in spot market activity due to canceled block space agreements.

Author: Rob Thubron
Title: LG verifies blue PHOLED tech, bringing the power-efficient, long-lasting "dream OLED" closer to market
Description: LG Display has become the first company to verify the commercialization of blue phosphorescent OLED (PHOLED) panels, a significant step towards more power-efficient and long-lasting OLED displays. By partnering with Universal Display Corp (UDC), LG has developed a dual-stack Tandem structure for blue PHOLED, leading to a 15% power saving compared to conventional OLED TVs. This innovation addresses the inefficiency and shorter lifespan of current blue OLED pixels, which contribute to screen burn-in, and is expected to be showcased at SID Display Week 2025 with applications in IT devices.
